label: First copy step (input = first original token, output = 2nd) in long sequences rich in r/o/f/p/h/l/g
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1 (recall_idx 1: the step right after <DEL>, where the fed-back first original token is the input and original token 1 is the output); 99.97% of activations and essentially all activation mass are at this step, and it never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Within that step it is selective (8.6% of such steps): the firing rate and magnitude rise steeply with sequence length (L=9 gives 51% of mass, L<=5 almost none) and with how many of the tokens r, o, f, p, h, l, g appear in the original sequence (output-token lift r 6.2x, o 5.5x, g 5.0x, l 4.7x; first token g 2.6x). This looks like a graded, distributed content dependence that no simple boolean captures well: recall_idx==1 alone gets about 100% recall at 8.6% precision, and the chosen predicate gets dev F1 0.43 with mass recall 0.68. It does not fire at later copy steps, at the delimiter, or on short sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 (+5.43), prev_tok=<DEL> (+5.43), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+2.81), orig4=f (+2.73), orig5=f (+2.41), orig3=r (+2.40). Lower it: to_go=2 (-3.20), orig3=v (-2.71), orig8=- (-2.51), out_tok=- (-2.47).
